item.title: Climate change can worsen income inequality
item.description: A study published in Sustainable Development that analyzed the relationship between climate change and income inequality for 23 emerging market economies from 2002 to 2022 found that greater climate pressure is positively associated with income inequality across three different inequality indicators (the Gini coefficient, the Palma ratio and the Theil index). Per capita income and institutional quality were negatively associated with inequality, whereas unemployment was positively associated with it. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Invasive plants show limited spread in Andalusia's mountains
item.description: A study by the University of Córdoba (UCO) departments of Forest Engineering and of Botany, Ecology and Plant Physiology reveals that the presence of invasive plants in Sierra Nevada and the Sierra de los Filabres—two mountain ecosystems in Andalusia that are especially vulnerable to climate change and home to unique plant species—is currently low. Specifically, invasive plants are most common in the areas closest to the edges of roads, and their presence declines at the highest points of the mountains. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: In Delhi, Hindu devotees congregated at the Yamuna River for the Chhath festival, wading through patches of toxic foam created by a mixture of pollutants including industrial chemicals and untreated sewage. item.title: How much CO₂ will stay? New study estimates long-term residual emissions under the EU Emissions Trading System
item.description: Current CO₂ emissions covered by the EU Emissions Trading System (EU-ETS1) could be substantially reduced by 2040. A new study by the Oeko-Institut, commissioned by Carbon Market Watch, examines the level of emissions that could remain in 2040 and 2050. In 2040, installations covered by the EU-ETS1—including waste incineration—could still emit between 159 and 231 million metric tons of CO₂. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: Researchers from Tulane University have observed a significant recovery in mangrove forests worldwide and their role in climate mitigation. item.title: León XIV se despide de Chiclayo y pide que nunca se acostumbren al sufrimiento de los demás
item.description: El Papa se ha despedido de Chiclayo con una visita a Zaña, una zona sin agua potable situada entre explanadas desérticas transformadas en basureros. En el último mensaje a su diócesis, ha recordado las lecciones que recibió de sus gentes durante los casi nueve años que pasó con ellos y les ha rogado «que nunca se acostumbren al sufrimiento de los demás».Zaña, antigua capital de Perú, custodia las ruinas del primer convento de América del Sur, centro espiritual de la región, que era de la Orden de los agustinos. A causa de los ataques piratas y de las inundaciones por el fenómeno de El Niño en… Fuente: ABC España - Internacional.
